title: 谷歌DeepMind为人工智能设计的蛋白质开发了隐形水印
content:
October 1, 2026 report
Google DeepMind develops invisible watermarks for AI-designed proteins
Paul Arnold
Author
Gaby Clark
Scientific Editor
Robert Egan
Senior Editor
Watermarks have long protected everything from bank notes and fine art to digital photographs and software, helping prove authenticity and trace an object's origin. Their main function is to protect copyright and verify authenticity.
That same traceability is needed in synthetic biology, where AI is now a useful research tool. To address this, Google DeepMind has introduced SynthIDBio, a method for embedding invisible signatures directly into biological sequences and 3D structures without interfering with their function.
AI is actively designing new functional proteins and predicting their three-dimensional shapes. But along with the benefits come a host of potential problems. These include biosecurity risks, such as the potential misuse of AI-designed biological molecules, and the spread of fake or misleading scientific data.
The team released details of its protein watermarking in a paper published in the journal Nature.
How to watermark a protein
There are two kinds of watermarks, digital patterns built directly into the protein design data. Which one is used depends on what the AI is generating. If the model is writing a protein sequence, the watermark is a secret code hidden in the order of the amino acids. If the model is predicting a 3D biomolecular structure, the watermark is an invisible pattern hidden in the 3D coordinates of the atoms.
Then came the jump from computer models to the real world. Researchers made watermarked protein binders in the lab to target three specific molecules. These included part of the coronavirus spike protein, a human protein involved in blood vessel growth and a human protein involved in regulating immune responses.
They then needed to find out two things. The first was whether the watermarks changed how the proteins work, and the second was whether a detector could spot them.
The watermarked proteins attached to all three targets with comparable strength to nonwatermarked versions. Meanwhile, the detection tool correctly identified all of the watermarked protein sequences and more than 99.8% of the watermarked 3D structures. Adding the watermarks did not significantly affect how well the proteins worked or the accuracy of the 3D structures.
There are still hurdles
While successful, the 3D structure watermark is not without its limits. The digital pattern can be destroyed when a design undergoes standard structural tweaks, a process known as relaxation. "However, robustness to relaxation is lacking, but we expect that this could be addressed by explicitly considering relaxation while training SynthIDBio-structure," wrote the researchers.
Despite those hurdles, the work could have applications in biosecurity and scientific integrity. "SynthIDBio presents a technical proof of concept that function- and quality-preserving biological watermarking is possible."
Researchers wanting to try the technology for themselves can find SynthIDBio-sequence's open-source code on GitHub.

report.summary: DeepMind发布SynthIDBio，可在AI设计蛋白质中嵌入隐形水印
report.background: 随着AI能设计功能蛋白并预测3D结构，合成生物学面临双重风险：生物分子可能被滥用，虚假科研数据也难溯源。传统水印保护钞票、艺术品和数字内容，但生物序列领域尚无成熟方案。DeepMind因此提出SynthIDBio，将签名直接嵌入氨基酸序列或原子坐标，不干扰功能。论文发表于Nature，并开源序列版代码。
key_points: SynthIDBio有两种水印：若生成蛋白质序列，水印是藏在氨基酸排列顺序中的秘密编码；若预测3D结构，水印是藏在原子坐标中的不可见图案。
研究团队在实验室制造了带水印的蛋白结合体，分别靶向新冠刺突蛋白片段、血管生长相关蛋白和免疫调控蛋白，结合强度与无水印版本相当。
检测工具能正确识别全部水印序列，并识别超过99.8%的水印3D结构；加入水印未显著影响蛋白功能或结构预测精度。
主要局限是3D结构水印在常规结构松弛优化后可能被破坏。作者认为，若在训练SynthIDBio-structure时显式考虑松弛，鲁棒性有望改善。
该技术有望用于生物安全和科研诚信，防止AI设计的生物分子被滥用或虚假数据传播；序列版开源代码已在GitHub发布。
report.impact: 对AI行业，水印可能成为AI生物设计模型的合规与溯源基础设施，推动生物安全治理。对开发者，序列版开源代码可快速试验，结构版需关注松弛鲁棒性。对普通用户，这能降低AI设计生物分子被滥用和虚假科研数据传播的风险，提升合成生物产品与论文可信度，但短期日常无直接感知。
report.tools: 可关注SynthIDBio-sequence的GitHub开源代码；阅读Nature论文DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10965-y；结合AlphaFold、RFdiffusion、ProteinMPNN等蛋白设计与结构预测工具，试验水印嵌入与检测流程。
